claim: Running main.py reports every code in codes.txt as invalid, including the well-formed ones.
why: load keeps the newline at the end of each line, and normalise removes only spaces, so the newline reaches is_valid. fullmatch needs the whole string to match, and the pattern has no way to consume a newline, so every line fails. The trap is that normalise sounds like it cleans the line, and that $ is known to match before a final newline.

deciding.note: normalise leaves the newline in place

false_confirms: (main\.py|is_valid).*(accept|pass|print\w* true|return\w* true|reported as valid).*ab-12|ab-12.*(is accepted|passes|prints? true|returns? true|reported as valid)

root.claim: main.py reports every code as invalid

atoms.claim: load keeps the trailing newline on each line
atoms.evidence: codes.py load returns lines unstripped; repr shows '\n'.

atoms.claim: normalise removes only spaces, so the newline survives
atoms.evidence: normalise calls rstrip with a single space; the repr output still ends in a newline.

atoms.claim: is_valid rejects a code that ends in a newline
atoms.evidence: fullmatch must consume the whole string; ran python3 main.py and all three print False.
